lessons.title: Upstream ctor switching from module-global to class-attribute hooks silently breaks ascend monkeypatch-swap subclasses
lessons.symptom: Ascend model subclass (e.g. vllm_ascend/models/qwen3_dflash2.py) activates its behavior by swapping a module global in the upstream parent's module during __init__; after an upstream refactor the draft model silently builds the wrong layers/selector (missing weights, degraded dflash2→dflash1) without any error.
lessons.root_cause: The ascend model activated its subclass behavior by temporarily rebinding module globals (dflash_mod.DFlashQwen3DecoderLayer / DFlashQwen3Model). Upstream refactored the ctors to read self.decoder_layer_cls / self.model_cls class attributes, so the rebinding no longer affects construction: plain DFlash1 layers are built (missing attention_conv/mlp_conv/candidate_selector weights) with no import error — pure silent degradation.
fix_guidance: When an upstream __init__ stops reading a module global, set the matching class attribute on the ascend subclass — it is inert on older pins where the parent still reads the global
Keep the module-global swap when the release pin (e.g. 0.27.1) predates the hook; it becomes inert on main, no vllm_version_is guard needed
Grep vllm_ascend/models for the same swap pattern (X = Y assignments to imported upstream modules) before declaring the fix complete

Note: ModelRegistry.register_model does dict assignment, so ascend plugin registrations overwrite upstream entries for the same arch name — duplicate registration of DFlash2DraftModel is not a conflict
lessons.example: step-1 @ vllm 27ec8ac6: upstream qwen3_dflash.py added decoder_layer_cls/model_cls (PR 52816); vllm_ascend/models/qwen3_dflash2.py swap hack went dead, fixed by adding decoder_layer_cls = DFlash2Qwen3DecoderLayer and model_cls = DFlash2Qwen3Model to the ascend subclasses while keeping the swap for the 0.27.1 pin.

lessons.title: Module-level patch().start() mocks die mid-batch when another UT file calls mock.patch.stopall() — re-arm in setUpClass
keywords: pipeline model parallel group is not initialized
lessons.symptom: UTs that construct objects calling distributed-group getters (get_pp_group/get_tp_group/...) fail with "pipeline model parallel group is not initialized" only in the shared-process batch (or intermittently by file order), while passing standalone.
lessons.root_cause: Module-level patch(...).start() mocks in one test file are global to the shared pytest process; any other file calling mock.patch.stopall() (e.g. to clean leaked patches) deactivates them, so tests that depend on those mocks fail only when batch execution order puts them after the stopall — order-dependent flakiness that does not reproduce when the file runs alone.
fix_guidance: Add a rearm helper that re-starts the same patches, and call it from setUpClass of every class whose tests depend on the mocks — setUpClass runs immediately before the class's tests, so no interleaved stopall can intervene
Do NOT call stop() in cleanup for re-armed patchers: after a foreign stopall() already stopped them, stop() raises RuntimeError; leaking them matches the file's existing module-level patch style
Source-side defensive getattr is the wrong fix when the invariant (initialized distributed groups) genuinely holds in production — fix the test's assumptions instead
Verify statically by grepping the attribute-access chain: the traceback frame naming the call site tells you which module namespace must hold the mock
lessons.example: step-1 fix round: tests/ut/kv_offload/test_mooncake_connector.py relied on module-level patch().start() for get_pp_group/get_pcp_group mocks; test_utils.py's test_enable_sp_uses_upstream_parallel_config calls mock.patch.stopall() mid-batch, so 5 thread-constructing tests failed with "pipeline model parallel group is not initialized". Fixed by rearm_group_patches() called in setUpClass of the three thread-constructing classes (no stop() — avoids double-stop RuntimeError after foreign stopall).

lessons.title: Diff-scoped mypy surfaces pre-existing test-file errors after the file enters the diff — fix per code, match file convention
lessons.symptom: After a fix round passes UT, the next mypy gate reports errors in the adapted test file at lines the fixer never touched (e.g. [list-item] on mock lists assigned to typed attributes, [method-assign] on method monkeypatches).
lessons.root_cause: The quality gate type-checks only files touched by the accumulated diff; a UT file adapted in a fix round carries pre-existing type errors that surface in the NEXT gate run, at lines unrelated to the actual edit — the fix must be mechanical per error code, not a re-analysis of the upstream patch.
fix_guidance: Expect the gate's mypy to be diff-scoped: adapting one file in a diff makes ALL its latent mypy errors visible, including lines you never touched

For [list-item] mock-list assignments, first grep the file for the same construct — if a convention like `# type: ignore[list-item]` already exists, match it instead of building real typed objects at only the new sites

For [method-assign] on __new__-constructed test objects, the assignment is genuine dynamic injection: `# type: ignore[method-assign]` is correct; if the line would exceed 120 chars, split the MagicMock(return_value=...) call to multiple lines with the ignore on the first line
Count the new ignore comments in the diff and require an exact match with the violation list (no strays = no stale ignores)
lessons.example: step-1 fix round 2: tests/ut/kv_offload/test_mooncake_connector.py — once the file entered the diff, mypy flagged 7x [list-item] (SimpleNamespace in group_transfer_info lists; the file already had 10 identical `types.SimpleNamespace(  # type: ignore[list-item]` instances) and 5x [method-assign] (MagicMock/lambda over methods on MooncakeConnectorWorker.__new__ bare objects). Matched the existing ignore convention; reformatted two MagicMock calls to multi-line to stay <=120.

lessons.title: E2E vllm can be newer than the step target — verify ascend overrides against the INSTALLED site-packages vllm, and shim renames via adapt_patch
lessons.symptom: E2E engine-core/worker crashes with signature/attribute errors (TypeError on overridden methods, AttributeError on upstream dataclass fields) that the vllm-upstream checkout at the step's target commit does NOT explain — e.g. `_get_logits() takes 3-4 positional arguments but 5 were given`, `'KVCacheTensor' object has no attribute 'shared_by'`, `'AscendMLAAttentionSpec' object has no attribute 'compress_ratio'`.
lessons.root_cause: The e2e environment runs an INSTALLED site-packages vllm ('dev') that is newer than the step's target checkout: main added `skip_gather` to LogitsProcessor.forward/_get_logits, renamed KVCacheTensor.shared_by to layers (adding layer_stride/block_stride), and dropped compress_ratio from MLAAttentionSpec. The vllm-upstream checkout is only a reference; tracebacks from site-packages are ground truth. Ascend has ~30 KVCacheTensor.shared_by read sites across 10 files (runners, mooncake connectors, kv_pool offload).
fix_guidance: Diff the failing API in /usr/local/python3.12.13/lib/python3.12/site-packages/vllm against the checkout before designing the fix — installed main wins
Signature additions with defaults (skip_gather): extend the ascend override and its private helpers, no version guard needed; mirror upstream's early-return semantics exactly

Field renames (shared_by→layers): install a class-level property alias in vllm_ascend/utils.py::_install_kv_cache_tensor_compat() called from adapt_patch() — vllm_ascend/__init__.py plugin entry points + platform/worker call adapt_patch in every process, so all ~30 read sites stay version-agnostic; guard the shim with vllm_version_is("0.27.1") and an idempotency isinstance(property) check; constructor-kwarg sites (recompute_cpu_offload/manager.py) need an explicit if/else with # type: ignore[call-arg] on the old branch and # type: ignore[attr-defined] on .shared_by reads in diff-scoped mypy
Base-class field removal (compress_ratio): redeclare the field with its default on the ascend subclass (pattern already used by AscendSlidingWindowMLASpec) — works on both lanes without a guard
lessons.example: step-1 e2e fix round: 5 suites failed on 3 drift signatures. Fixed in 4 files: utils.py (shared_by property shim via adapt_patch), ops/vocab_parallel_embedding.py (skip_gather threaded through _get_logits/_get_logits_lmheadtp/_get_logits_normal), core/kv_cache_interface.py (compress_ratio: int = 1 on AscendMLAAttentionSpec), recompute_cpu_offload/manager.py (guarded KVCacheTensor construction).

lessons.title: Property alias shimming a renamed dataclass field must detect the rename on the class — a version guard alone shadows the real field on main snapshots that still carry it and breaks construction
keywords: property of 'KVCacheTensor' object has no setter
lessons.symptom: After installing a `KVCacheTensor.shared_by = property(getter)` compat alias (guarded only by vllm_version_is("0.27.1")), 30 UTs fail with `AttributeError: property of 'KVCacheTensor' object has no setter` at the dataclass-generated `<string>:N in __init__` whenever tests construct `KVCacheTensor(..., shared_by=[...])` — while the same shim works fine in the e2e environment.
lessons.root_cause: The gate environments run DIFFERENT main snapshots: the UT env's main vllm still HAS the shared_by dataclass field; the e2e env's newer main renamed it to layers. vllm_version_is("0.27.1") is False on BOTH mains, so the version guard cannot distinguish them. On the UT env the property (a data descriptor) shadows the real field: the dataclass __init__'s `self.shared_by = ...` hits the setter-less property. Any property alias for a renamed field must be a no-op wherever the original field still exists.
fix_guidance: Detect the rename on the class, not the version string: install the alias only when `hasattr(KVCacheTensor, "layers") and not hasattr(KVCacheTensor, "shared_by")`
Give the alias property both getter and setter (lambda self, value: setattr(self, "layers", value)) so writes/dataclass paths stay workable where it IS installed

Constructor-kwarg call sites must use the same class-level discriminator: `hasattr(KVCacheTensor, "layers")` picks the layers kwarg, else shared_by — never vllm_version_is for this rename (the alias itself installs a shared_by attribute, which would fool a hasattr(shared_by) check after adapt_patch runs; hasattr(layers) is shim-proof)
Keep # type: ignore[attr-defined] on .shared_by reads and [call-arg] on the old-lane kwarg for diff-scoped mypy against the renamed vllm
lessons.example: step-1 fix round 4: round-3's version-guarded shared_by property shim broke 30 UTs constructing KVCacheTensor(shared_by=...) because the UT env's main still has the field. Fixed by feature-detecting the rename in _install_kv_cache_tensor_compat (utils.py) and switching recompute_cpu_offload/manager.py's construction guard to hasattr(KVCacheTensor, "layers").

lessons.title: The e2e harness may pin VLLM_VERSION to the release tag while running main vllm code — never gate a mid-main API rename shim on vllm_version_is; feature-detect the rename on the class
lessons.symptom: A compat shim (KVCacheTensor.shared_by property alias) that works in UT fails to install in e2e: both e2e rounds keep failing with `'KVCacheTensor' object has no attribute 'shared_by'` even though the shim's feature gate would pass on the e2e vllm (which has `layers`, no `shared_by`); meanwhile guard-free fixes in the same round (skip_gather, compress_ratio) DO take effect on e2e.
lessons.root_cause: `vllm_version_is("0.27.1")` reads `envs_ascend.VLLM_VERSION` first, and the e2e harness pins VLLM_VERSION=0.27.1 (the release tag) while the installed vllm is main code (0.28.1rc1.dev221 with the rename). So every `vllm_version_is("0.27.1")` early-return inside the shim fired on e2e and the alias never installed. The UT env does not pin VLLM_VERSION (vllm.__version__=0.28.1rc1.dev... → False), which is why the same guard let the shim install there (and shadow the real field in round 3).
fix_guidance: Remove any vllm_version_is early-return from mid-main rename shims — the version signal is unreliable in both directions: e2e pins VLLM_VERSION=0.27.1 over main code, UT runs unpinned dev versions

Detect the rename on the class: install the property alias only when `hasattr(KVCacheTensor, "layers") and not hasattr(KVCacheTensor, "shared_by")` — this is correct on the release lane, main snapshots before the rename, and main snapshots after it, under any VLLM_VERSION
Discriminate constructor-kwarg call sites with `hasattr(KVCacheTensor, "layers")` too (shim-proof: the alias installs shared_by, never layers)

When a fix works in UT but not e2e (or vice versa), compare the env matrices: VLLM_VERSION pinning, installed vllm snapshot (site-packages/vllm/_version.py + dist-info), and which guards are version-gated vs guard-free — the guard-free ones are the control group
lessons.example: step-1 fix round 5: rounds 3-4's shims were correct feature-wise but kept the vllm_version_is("0.27.1") early return, which fired on e2e (harness pins VLLM_VERSION=0.27.1) so the alias never installed there. Removing the version check fixed e2e while the feature gate still protected UT (no shadowing) and the release lane.
